newsitem.title: UK: Tomkins slips as buy-back hopes dashed.
newsitem.headline: Tomkins slips as buy-back hopes dashed.

text.p: Shares in Tomkins Plc retreated from their early gains on Monday, pulled back by profit-taking after recent gains and disappointment that the company was not planning a share buy-back, traders said.

The engineering-to-baking group announced half-year pre-tax profits of 168.8 million stg, above analysts' forecasts which averaged 160 million. But executive chairman Greg Hutchings said the firm was not likely to return its cash pile to shareholders, preferring to look for acquisitions instead.
By 1300 GMT the stock was down 3-1/2p at 274, after reaching a three-month high of 288 earlier in the wake of the results.
"The shares have had a good run and they were great results and a lot of people would have been looking to take profits now," one market-maker said.
"But the main thing is that the chairman has knocked speculation about a share buy-back on the head," he said. "There's been a lot of speculation about that recently."
Hutchings told a press briefing after the results that he was puzzled by the level of investor demand for Tomkins shares and blamed anti-conglomerate sentiment in the UK market.
